messages:
maya: Heads-up — I wired up a comparison dashboard for batch-scheduler vs continuous kernel selection across the /generate and /chat routes. Seeing a weird token-latency shift during the v2 canary.
sam: Nice. Link? :eyes:
maya: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/perm/batch-vs-continuous?orgId=1 — top panel is token-level p50/p95 breakdown, bottom is per-route qps and kv-cache hit rate.
raj: Quick summary of what you saw?
maya: p50 stable, but p95 on /chat bumped ~12-18ms for a subset of traces during kernel switch at 10:17 UTC. The traces that regressed all have seq_len <= 64 and high KV cache miss spikes.
leah: Could be kernel choice causing more memory traffic for short sequences. Did you correlate with kernel selection logs?
maya: Yep — added a small tag to logs. If kernel=continuous we see higher memcpy counts and longer tail when kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.7. Example PromQL I used:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model_version))
/
sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (route, model_version)
```
sam: Can you paste the exact trace IDs for a couple of regressed requests?
maya: trace ids: 7f9b3a, 8c4d1e, 9a2e5f — attached lightweight flamegraphs on the dashboard.
infra-bot: Canary rollout started for model v2 -> v2.1 at 2028-06-02T10:15:00Z
raj: Interesting that only v2.1 canary is affected. Does v2 (stable) use a different kernel selection policy?
maya: v2 stable pinned to legacy-batcher, v2.1 defaulting to auto-kernel with prefer_continuous for small seq lengths. If I force legacy-batcher for v2.1, tails disappear.
leah: Hmm. That suggests batcher heuristics + cache interplay. Could be microbatch aggregation causing additional copying when cache misses occur.
sam: Any change in batching window / max_batch_size between versions?
maya: v2 had max_batch_size=64 and window_ms=5. v2.1 uses adaptive window (0-10ms) and max_batch_size=128. I rolled a canary with max_batch_size=64 + adaptive window off and latency p95 dropped back down.
raj: KV cache hit rate drop — what's the root cause? Prefetching disabled on canary or eviction policy changed?
maya: We changed the KV prefetch to LRU-2 in v2.1 to improve cold-starts. Side effect: transiently higher evictions under bursty traffic, leading to more backend lookup and memcpy.
leah: Action items?
maya: 1) Revert kernel selection policy for canary to legacy-batcher while we iterate (done). 2) Add metric: kernel_selector_decision{model_version, route, seq_len_bucket}. 3) Add kv_evictions_total with labels for pool and model_version. 4) Add quick dashboard card comparing p95 by kernel per-route.
sam: Also add synthetic canary load with short sequences to CI perf job. I can add a smoke test that asserts p95 delta < 5ms.
raj: Agree. Also record alloc and memcpy counters at token-level for those traces so we can attribute tail to copies vs compute.
maya: I've pushed a small patch to the dashboard and new instrumented metrics are in staging. Dashboard link (staging): https://staging-dash.redwood.internal/d/perm/batch-vs-continuous?panelId=7
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline for staging finished: build-3311 -> serving-canary-staging
leah: For the rollout decision — since we reverted kernel policy, what's recommended next for the canary? Continue with v2.1 if we keep legacy-batcher, or block until we fix prefetch/LRU-2?
sam: Block rollout of auto-kernel until we have kv_evictions_total + memcpy attribution. If we keep legacy-batcher then canary can proceed with other changes.
maya: I'll open a short PR for the metric additions and add an entry in eng-runtime checklist. Also added a perf note in the dashboard panel describing the root cause hypothesis.
raj: Good. Can we also add a per-route alert when p95 delta between model_versions > 10ms and kv_cache_hit_rate drops > 5%? Better to catch regressions quickly.
leah: I'll add that alert in the next ops runbook.
maya: Thanks all — I'll follow up with the PR link and a short postmortem if needed. :thumbsup:
